question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

If I hand her a flower and say, “Give it to mamma,” she take it to her mother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. takes it.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is a conditional sentence of Type 1 (real/probable condition), whose structure is: If + Subject + V1/V5 (simple present), Subject + will/simple present + V1.

• The "if" clause here uses the simple present ("If I hand her a flower and say ..."), so the main clause must also be in the simple present.

• The subject "she" is a third-person singular subject, so the verb must take "-s/-es" → "takes", not "take".

◦ Correct: If I hand her a flower and say, "Give it to mamma," she takes it to her mother.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "was taking it" (past continuous) wrongly shifts the sentence into the past.

• Option 3 "had took it" is doubly wrong — after "had" the past participle (V3) "taken" is needed, not "took".

• Option 4 "had taken it" (past perfect) again breaks the present-tense sequence of the sentence.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement rule: singular subject → singular verb (he/she/it goes, takes, writes); plural subject → plural verb (they go, take, write).

• Tense sequence: within one sentence the tenses of the clauses must agree unless there is a clear reason to shift. Here both clauses describe a general/habitual fact, so both stay in the simple present.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Divergent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Similar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Divergent" (adjective) means differing from each other; moving or extending in different directions; dissimilar. (भिन्न / अलग-अलग दिशाओं में जाने वाला)

◦ Example: The two brothers had divergent views on politics.

• Its antonym is "Similar", which means alike, resembling one another, of the same kind. (समान)

◦ Example: The twins have very similar tastes in music.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Addition" (the act of adding something) is unrelated to the idea of difference.

• Option 3 "Disrespectful" (showing a lack of respect) is unrelated.

• Option 4 "Obvious" (clear, easily seen) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of divergent: differing, dissimilar, conflicting, disparate, deviating, contrasting.

• Antonyms of divergent: similar, alike, convergent, identical, same, uniform.

• Related words: diverge (verb — to separate and go in different directions), divergence (noun), converge (verb — to come together at a point).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

To much seriousness hardens the world, pinning it down with rules.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. to much.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is one of spelling/word choice. The intended word is the adverb of degree "too" (meaning "excessively, more than needed"), not the preposition "to".

◦ Correct: Too much seriousness hardens the world, pinning it down with rules.

• "Too much" = an excessive quantity/degree; "to" is a preposition or the marker of an infinitive (to go, to the market).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "hardens the" is correct — the uncountable subject "seriousness" is singular and takes the singular verb "hardens".

• "world, pinning" is correct — "pinning it down with rules" is a participial phrase properly modifying the preceding clause.

• "with rules" is correct — "pin down with" takes the preposition "with" for the instrument/means.

NOTE

• Commonly confused homophones: to (preposition/infinitive marker), too (also / excessively), two (the number 2).

◦ She is too tired to walk. / He gave the book to me. / I have two pens.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

He managed to save his father’s business by the sweat of his brow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. hard work.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "by the sweat of one's brow" means by one's own hard physical labour or strenuous effort. (कड़ी मेहनत से / अपने परिश्रम से)

◦ Example: He built this house by the sweat of his brow.

• In the sentence, he saved his father's business through hard work, so Option 2 is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "incidentally" (by chance / by the way) contradicts the idea of deliberate effort.

• Option 3 "tricks and strategies" suggests cunning, not honest toil.

• Option 4 "any way possible" suggests using any means, which is not the sense of the idiom.

NOTE

• Related idioms of hard work: "burn the midnight oil" (to work late into the night), "put one's shoulder to the wheel" (to work hard), "work one's fingers to the bone" (to work extremely hard), "leave no stone unturned" (to try every possible way).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

A place where water is collected and stored for future use.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Reservoir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Reservoir" is a large natural or artificial lake/tank where water is collected and stored for future use (for drinking, irrigation or generating electricity). (जलाशय)

◦ Example: The city's reservoir was full after the monsoon rains.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Aquarium" — a glass tank in which fish and water plants are kept.

• Option 2 "Resort" — a place people visit for holidays and relaxation.

• Option 3 "Sanatorium" — a hospital/establishment for the treatment of chronically ill or convalescing patients.

NOTE

• Other useful one-word substitutes: Reservoir (store of water), Granary (store for grain), Arsenal/Armoury (store for weapons), Aviary (place for birds), Apiary (place for bees), Dairy (place where milk products are made).

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The new chairman of the company announced attracted bonus for the employees on the occasion of the new year.
option_2: announced an attractive bonus for the employees
option_3: announcing attracted bonus for the employees
option_4: announced attracting bonus for the employees
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. announced an attractive bonus for the employees.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed in the underlined part:

◦ The adjective must be "attractive" (appealing, tempting), not the past participle "attracted" (drawn towards something). A bonus is attractive; a person is attracted.

◦ The singular countable noun "bonus" needs the article "an" before the vowel sound of "attractive".

• Correct: The new chairman of the company announced an attractive bonus for the employees on the occasion of the new year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement required" is wrong because the sentence as printed is ungrammatical.

• Option 3 "announcing" is a participle, leaving the sentence without a finite main verb.

• Option 4 "attracting bonus" wrongly uses the present participle; "attracting" would mean "the bonus is drawing something", which is not the intended sense.

NOTE

• -ed vs -ing adjectives: the "-ing" form describes the thing causing the feeling (an exciting match, an attractive offer); the "-ed" form describes the person feeling it (an excited crowd, an attracted buyer).

• Use "a" before a consonant sound and "an" before a vowel sound: an attractive bonus, an hour, a university.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) The institute / (B) have been / (C) divided into / (D) multiple departments
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "The institute", a singular collective noun. A singular subject takes the singular auxiliary "has", not the plural "have".

◦ Correct: The institute has been divided into multiple departments.

• Part (B) "have been" therefore contains the error.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Part (A) "The institute" is correct — a properly formed noun phrase with the definite article.

• Part (C) "divided into" is correct — the verb "divide" takes the preposition "into" (divided into parts).

• Part (D) "multiple departments" is correct — the plural noun follows the determiner "multiple".

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: singular subject → has/is/was; plural subject → have/are/were.

• Collective nouns such as institute, committee, team, jury, government are usually treated as singular in Indian/British academic usage when the body acts as a single unit.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

They allowed us to powder by crushing the spices, pick over the raisins and lick the stirring spoons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. grind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To "grind" means to reduce something to small particles or powder by crushing it (between two hard surfaces, in a mill or with a pestle). (पीसना)

◦ Correct: They allowed us to grind the spices, pick over the raisins and lick the stirring spoons.

• The underlined group "powder by crushing" is exactly the definition of grind.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "gain" — to obtain or acquire something.

• Option 2 "greet" — to welcome or address someone politely.

• Option 3 "guess" — to estimate without sufficient information.

NOTE

• Verb forms: grind – ground – ground (irregular verb). E.g., "She ground the coffee beans."

• Related kitchen verbs: crush (to press and break), mince (to chop very finely), knead (to work dough with the hands), whisk (to beat rapidly).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Mild
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Gentle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mild" means not severe or harsh; gentle, moderate, soft in nature or effect. (हल्का / सौम्य)

◦ Example: He has a mild temperament and never shouts.

• Its closest synonym is "Gentle", meaning mild, kind and not harsh or violent. (कोमल)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Scathing" (severely critical, harsh in criticism) is an antonym.

• Option 2 "Brittle" (hard but easily broken) is unrelated.

• Option 4 "Severe" (very great, harsh, strict) is a clear antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of mild: gentle, moderate, soft, tender, placid, temperate, bland.

• Antonyms of mild: severe, harsh, extreme, violent, fierce, intense, scathing.

• "Mild" also describes weather (mild winter = not very cold) and food (mild curry = not spicy).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Instead of answering the question directly, the politician kept ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. beating around the bush.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to beat around the bush" means to avoid coming to the main point; to talk in a roundabout, evasive way. (घुमा-फिराकर बात करना)

◦ Correct: Instead of answering the question directly, the politician kept beating around the bush.

• The phrase "instead of answering ... directly" is a direct clue to evasive talk.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "crying over spilt milk" = regretting something that has already happened and cannot be changed.

• Option 2 "pointing at his laurels" is not a standard idiom; the correct one is "resting on one's laurels" (relying on past achievements).

• Option 4 "spilling the bean" is incorrectly formed; the idiom is "to spill the beans" (to reveal a secret).

NOTE

• Related idioms: "come to the point" / "get down to brass tacks" (to speak directly) are the opposite of beating around the bush.

• Idioms must be used in their fixed form — the words cannot be changed or made singular/plural at will.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Rishi asked Karan will he get a new football for him?
option_1: would he get a new football for him?
option_2: if he would get a new football for him.
option_3: if would he get a new football for him?
option_4: if he will get a new football for him?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. if he would get a new football for him.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a sentence in indirect (reported) speech. Three rules apply:

◦ An interrogative sentence beginning with a helping verb is reported using the conjunction "if/whether".

◦ In indirect speech the question form is dropped — the word order becomes subject + verb, and the sentence ends with a full stop, not a question mark.

◦ The reporting verb "asked" is in the past, so "will" is back-shifted to "would".

• Correct: Rishi asked Karan if he would get a new football for him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps the interrogative word order ("would he get") and the question mark — both wrong in reported speech.

• Option 3 "if would he get ... ?" retains the inverted order and the question mark.

• Option 4 fails to back-shift "will" to "would" and keeps the question mark.

NOTE

• Direct → Indirect back-shift of tenses: will → would, can → could, may → might, is/am → was, has/have → had, do/does → did.

• Yes/No questions are reported with "if/whether"; Wh-questions are reported with the same wh-word (He asked me where I lived).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Retrospact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Retrospact" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Retrospect", meaning a survey or review of a past course of events; looking back on the past. (पूर्वदृष्टि / पिछली बातों पर विचार)

◦ Example: In retrospect, I should have accepted that job offer.

• Spelling key: RETRO (backwards) + SPECT (to look) → "to look back".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Omitted" (left out) — correctly spelt; note the double "t" because the stress falls on the last syllable of "omit".

• "Conscience" (the inner sense of right and wrong) — correctly spelt; remember SCIENCE inside con-science.

• "Admission" (the act of admitting or entering) — correctly spelt with double "s".

NOTE

• The Latin root spect/spec = "to look": inspect, prospect, spectator, spectacles, perspective, retrospect.

• Do not confuse conscience (noun — moral sense) with conscious (adjective — awake/aware).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Often
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rarely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Often" is an adverb of frequency meaning many times; frequently. (अक्सर)

◦ Example: She often visits her grandparents.

• Its antonym is "Rarely", meaning not often; seldom; on very few occasions. (कभी-कभार / विरले ही)

◦ Example: He rarely watches television.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Generally" (usually, in most cases) is close in meaning to "often", not opposite.

• Option 3 "Periodically" (from time to time, at regular intervals) is not an antonym.

• Option 4 "Usually" (normally, most of the time) is a synonym of often.

NOTE

• Adverbs of frequency arranged from highest to lowest: always → usually → often → sometimes → occasionally → seldom/rarely → never.

• Synonyms of often: frequently, repeatedly, regularly, commonly. Antonyms: rarely, seldom, infrequently, never.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The boy whose the sister is ill has left.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. whose the sister.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Whose" is a possessive relative pronoun, and it is itself a determiner. Therefore it is never followed by an article (a/an/the) before the noun.

◦ Incorrect: The boy whose the sister is ill has left.

◦ Correct: The boy whose sister is ill has left.

• The structure is: whose + noun (whose sister, whose book, whose father).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The boy" is correct — a properly formed noun phrase.

• "is ill" is correct — singular subject "sister" with singular verb "is".

• "has left" is correct — the present perfect with the singular subject "The boy".

NOTE

• Relative pronouns: who (subject — person), whom (object — person), whose (possessive — person/thing), which (thing), that (person/thing).

• Similarly, no article is used after other determiners: "my the book" ✗ → "my book" ✓.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

A strong _________ for mathematics and problem-solving can be very useful.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. aptitude.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aptitude" means a natural ability or talent for learning or doing something. It collocates naturally with "for" — an aptitude for mathematics. (योग्यता / नैसर्गिक क्षमता)

◦ Correct: A strong aptitude for mathematics and problem-solving can be very useful.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "strength" would be redundant after "A strong ..." and does not take "for" in this sense.

• Option 3 "functioning" (the way something works/operates) does not fit a personal ability.

• Option 4 "perception" (the way one notices or understands something) takes "of", not "for", and does not mean natural talent.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: an aptitude for languages, a talent for music, a flair for design, a knack for fixing things.

• Related: aptitude test — an examination designed to measure a person's natural ability for a particular kind of work or study.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Priviledge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Priviledge" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Privilege" — a special right, advantage or immunity granted to a particular person or group. (विशेषाधिकार)

◦ Example: Education should be a right, not a privilege.

• Spelling key: PRI + VI + LEGE — there is no "d" in the word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Recommendation" (a suggestion or endorsement) — correctly spelt: one "c", double "m".

• "Affiliate" (to officially attach or connect to an organisation) — correctly spelt: double "f", one "l".

• "Parachute" (a device used to slow descent through the air) — correctly spelt.

NOTE

• The word privilege comes from Latin privus (private) + lex/legis (law) — literally "a private law".

• Frequently misspelt words in SSC exams: privilege, occurrence, accommodation, embarrassment, maintenance, questionnaire, harassment, committee.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

My manager forced me to resign from my job as a chef since I underwent a spine surgery. I was depressed and had lost all hope. Later my father motivated me to open my own café and showed me ways to be independent. After all it is true that one should not ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cry over spilt milk.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to cry over spilt milk" means to waste time regretting or lamenting something bad that has already happened and cannot be undone. (बीती बातों पर पछताना)

◦ Correct: After all it is true that one should not cry over spilt milk.

• The context — losing a job, then moving on to start a café — perfectly matches the advice not to brood over past misfortune.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "grease the palm" = to bribe someone.

• Option 2 "blow one's own trumpet" = to boast about one's own achievements.

• Option 4 "blow hot and cold" = to keep changing one's opinion or attitude.

NOTE

• Related idioms about moving on: "let bygones be bygones" (to forget past quarrels), "turn over a new leaf" (to start afresh), "what's done is done".

• Full proverb form: "It is no use crying over spilt milk."

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.

He was quaking in his boots when he had to give a speech on the stage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To tremble with fear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to quake/shake in one's boots" means to tremble or shiver with fear; to be extremely frightened or nervous. (डर से काँपना)

◦ Correct: He was quaking in his boots (= trembling with fear) when he had to give a speech on the stage.

• Stage fright before public speaking is a classic context for this idiom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 4 ("in excitement") and Option 2 ("in happiness") give a positive emotion, whereas the idiom always expresses fear.

• The verb "quake" itself means to shake or tremble (as in "earthquake").

NOTE

• Other idioms expressing fear: "get cold feet" (to lose courage at the last moment), "have one's heart in one's mouth" (to be very frightened), "make one's blood run cold", "scared stiff", "jump out of one's skin".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

If I will get good marks, my father will buy me a laptop.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. get.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a Conditional Sentence Type 1 (a real, likely future condition). Its structure is:

◦ If + Subject + V1 (simple present), Subject + will + V1

• The golden rule is that "will" is never used in the "if" clause; the simple present is used there instead, even though the meaning is future.

◦ Correct: If I get good marks, my father will buy me a laptop.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No substitution required" is wrong because "If I will get" violates the conditional rule.

• Option 2 "am getting" (present continuous) does not suit a condition about examination results.

• Option 3 "gets" is wrong in subject–verb agreement — the subject is "I", which takes "get", not "gets".

NOTE

• The three main conditionals:

◦ Type 1 (real/possible): If + simple present, will + V1 — "If it rains, we will cancel the trip."

◦ Type 2 (unreal present): If + simple past, would + V1 — "If I had money, I would travel."

◦ Type 3 (unreal past): If + had + V3, would have + V3 — "If he had studied, he would have passed."

question:
Four words of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a spelling error.

Human activities that release longlived greenhouse gases into the atmosphere also leed to the enhancement of concentrations of shorterlived ozone and particulate matter in the atmosphere.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. leed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Leed" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "lead" (verb — to result in, to bring about, to guide). (कारण बनना / ले जाना)

◦ Correct: Human activities that release longlived greenhouse gases into the atmosphere also lead to the enhancement of concentrations of shorterlived ozone and particulate matter in the atmosphere.

• "Lead to" is a fixed collocation meaning "to result in".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "release" (to let out / set free) — correctly spelt.

• "concentrations" (the amount of a substance present in a given space) — correctly spelt.

• "particulate" (relating to tiny separate particles, as in particulate matter/PM2.5) — correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Note the pronunciation trap: lead (verb, /liːd/ — to guide) vs lead (noun, /led/ — the metal Pb) vs led (past tense of the verb lead).

◦ "He leads the team." / "She led the team last year." / "The pipe is made of lead."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. chemicals.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank continues the list of beneficial substances found in fruits and vegetables — "vitamins, minerals and plant ________".

• "Plant chemicals" (also called phytochemicals) is the standard expression for the natural compounds in plants that benefit health. (पादप रसायन)

◦ Correct: Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant chemicals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "residue" (what is left over, often waste) has a negative sense and would not be listed among "important" nutrients.

• Option 2 "bacteria" are micro-organisms, not plant constituents of this kind.

• Option 4 "organisms" are living beings, not substances contained in food.

NOTE

• Vocabulary note: phytochemicals (from Greek phyto = plant) include antioxidants such as carotenoids, flavonoids and lycopene, which help protect against disease.

• In cloze (fill-in-the-blank) passages, always use parallelism — the missing word must belong to the same category as the other items in the list.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. varieties.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Varieties" means different kinds or types of the same thing. The sentence says there are many different types of fruits and vegetables available. (किस्में / प्रकार)

◦ Correct: There are many varieties of fruits and vegetables available ...

• The word also links forward to "aim for variety" later in the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "traits" (distinguishing qualities of a person or thing) does not mean "kinds".

• Option 2 "characters" refers to personal qualities or to people in a story — wrong register here.

• Option 4 "uses" would clash with the following clause "and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them", which already covers usage.

NOTE

• Collocation: "a variety of", "varieties of rice/mangoes", "for the sake of variety".

• "Variety is the spice of life" — a well-known proverb meaning new and varied experiences make life interesting.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. rich.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed collocation is "rich in" — meaning containing a large amount of something. A diet rich in fruit and vegetables = a diet containing plenty of them. (से भरपूर)

◦ Correct: A diet rich in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "immersed" means deeply absorbed/submerged (immersed in work) — wrong sense for a diet.

• Option 3 "content" as an adjective means satisfied; the noun "content" would need a different structure ("the content of ...").

• Option 4 "varied" would need "in" to be dropped — "a varied diet" is correct, but "a diet varied in fruit" is not idiomatic.

NOTE

• Adjective + preposition collocations: rich in minerals, poor in nutrients, full of energy, deficient in vitamins, abundant in resources.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. enough.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enough" means as much as is necessary; sufficient. The sentence points out a shortfall: most Indians do not eat the sufficient/recommended quantity of fruit and vegetables. (पर्याप्त)

◦ Correct: Most Indians do not eat enough fruit and vegetables.

• It follows naturally from the previous sentence, which prescribes five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "some" is normally avoided in negative sentences ("do not eat any" would be used instead) and does not convey the idea of a shortfall against a standard.

• Option 3 "many" is used with countable plural nouns, but "fruit" here is used as an uncountable noun.

• Option 4 "plenty" requires the preposition "of" — "plenty of fruit" — so it cannot fill the blank as it stands.

NOTE

• "Enough" goes after an adjective/adverb (good enough, fast enough) but before a noun (enough food, enough time).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. nutrients.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nutrients" are the substances in food (vitamins, minerals, proteins, etc.) that living things need to grow and stay healthy. (पोषक तत्त्व)

◦ Correct: ... aim for variety to get the most nutrients and appeal.

• The whole passage is about the health value of fruits and vegetables, so eating a variety gives the maximum nutrients as well as visual/taste appeal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "assortment" (a mixed collection) merely repeats the idea of "variety" already stated in the same sentence.

• Option 2 "fun" does not fit a nutrition-based passage.

• Option 4 "advancement" (progress or promotion) is completely out of context.

NOTE

• Nutrients are classified as macronutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats) and micronutrients (vitamins and minerals).

• Related words: nutrition (the process of taking in food), nutritious (adjective — full of nutrients), malnutrition (lack of proper nutrition).
